rappel_detail.notes: Below the rappel it is a scree and talus scramble worked rightward — clockwise around the peak, roughly south then west — back into the basin and the packs at the base of the west face. Terrain under the horn is low-angle enough that some parties downclimb it instead of rappelling.
rappel_detail.anchor: A natural horn wrapped in webbing / in-situ slings on the east side of the summit block. No bolts. It is re-slung periodically because it is the standard anchor for every CBR route that tops out here, so what you find will be a mix of ages.
hazards: The upper pitches and the ground around the summit block are loose and lichen-covered — the reason parties are advised to stay roped rather than solo across to the anchor
Single natural anchor on a high-traffic descent: inspect the webbing and add or replace your own before loading it
rappel_detail.station: From the top of the route, scramble across to the east side of the summit block; the slung horn is on that side and the rappel drops eastward. If you skip the balanced-rock boulder problem you can bypass the block entirely and never touch this anchor.

set.rappels: Finish over the top and take the standard Colchuck Balanced Rock descent: one rappel of about 30 m east off a slung horn on the summit block, then scree clockwise around the peak. To bail low, rappel the route from natural anchors and the fixed pitons with a 60 m rope.
